threshold_sweep.note: F1 assumes a false positive and a false negative are equally bad. The cost-optimal threshold uses the supplied asymmetry and is the one an operator should actually deploy.

calibration_report.rationale: Selected on expected calibration error, not on AUC: calibration is a monotone transform, so it barely moves ranking metrics but decides whether the probability can be multiplied by a dollar amount.

split.rationale: Rows are exchangeable (no time or group structure), so a random 20% hold-out is unbiased. Stratified on the target to hold the positive rate constant across folds.

economics.source: Illustrative but conventional telco assumptions: 30% contribution margin, a $45 retention incentive accepted by roughly a third of those offered, and an 18-month remaining-life horizon.
economics.cost_model: A false negative forfeits the recoverable margin (lifetime margin x acceptance rate), not the whole lifetime margin -- an offer only works some of the time. A false positive costs one wasted incentive. The same model drives the threshold sweep and the campaign simulation.
economics.interpretation: Missing a recoverable churner costs about 2.7x a wasted incentive, which puts the cost-optimal threshold at 0.27 rather than 0.50.

campaign_simulation.interpretation: Contacting the top 35% by predicted risk reaches 74% of churners and nets $11,597 on the 1,409-customer hold-out. Contacting everyone destroys value because most incentives go to customers who were never going to leave.

baselines.name: Predict base rate for everyone
baselines.description: Constant 0.265; the floor any model must clear.
